comments.author: Reedx
comments.story_title: Ray Dalio AMA
comments.why_zh: Dalio 对经济的通俗讲解。
comments.quote_zh: 如果你还没看过他的视频《经济机器是如何运行的》，我强烈推荐
comments.text_zh: 如果你还没看过他的视频《经济机器是如何运行的》，我强烈推荐：[VIDEO]。另外，他经营 Bridgewater 的方式也非常有意思。它的组织目标就是让最好的想法浮现出来，并判断哪些观点最可能是正确的。这是一种“想法精英制”，也是一种极端透明的文化。一切都被记录下来，并向公司里所有人开放。员工非常坦率，甚至对 CEO（Ray）也毫不留情地直言。他说很多人在头一年左右就流失了，但留下来适应了的人都很喜欢这种文化，无法想象还能用别的方式工作。他在 TED 演讲里相当详细地讲了这一切是如何运作的：[LINK]。他的书 Principles 奠定了这套基础。节选：[LINK]。视频：[LINK]
comments.text: If you haven't seen his video, How the Economic Machine Works, I highly recommend it: [VIDEO] Also the way he runs Bridgewater is really interesting. It's structured with the goal to surface the best ideas and figure out which opinions are most likely to be correct. It's an "idea meritocracy" and a culture of radical transparency. Everything is recorded and made available to everyone else in the company. Employees are very candid, brutally honest, even with the CEO (Ray). He says a lot of people churn out in the first year or so, but those that get used to it love it and can't imagine working another way. His Ted Talk goes into quite a bit of detail about how it all works: [LINK] His book Principles lays out the foundation. Excerpt: [LINK] Videos: [LINK]

comments.author: icu
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What is really wrong with the US economy, really?
comments.why_zh: 在去杠杆相关资料中被列出。
comments.quote_zh: 更多信息请看以下内容
comments.text_zh: 这里的问题有好几个层面。我过去 5 年一直在专门研究到底发生了什么，所以我尽量把它浓缩一下。从“较短”的商业周期视角（不到 10 年的跨度）来看，问题在于我们不是处在衰退中，而是处在去杠杆中。二战以来我们就没经历过一次去杠杆，所以大多数人不知道那是什么，以为它是衰退。去杠杆是百年一遇的大规模财富转移事件。我在这个回复末尾放了一些关于什么是去杠杆的资料。长期的问题是，美联储是一家私人银行。这意味着美国政府和美国公民并不控制美联储。别被它看起来像政府分支的那层外衣骗了，尤其是那套由总统任命美联储主席的把戏。它是一家私人银行，可以印钱再卖给美国政府，而美国公民被迫使用这些钱。这意味着美国政府和美国公民都是奴隶，对自己的未来毫无掌控权。每印出一美元，都是压在美国人民身上的一笔债务，也是对当前货币价值的一次贬值。本质上，可以把印钱想成美联储把钱从你口袋里转移到他们口袋里的方式。此外，我认为美联储操纵经济周期，制造出财富转移事件，然后从中获利。更多信息请看以下内容：[VIDEO] [LINK] www.youtube.com/watch?v=mII9NZ8MMVM [LINK] [LINK]
comments.text: There are several levels to what is wrong. I have dedicated the last 5 years to discovering what is going on so I will try my best to condense it down. In terms of a 'shorter' business cycle view (less than 10 year perspective) to what is wrong is that we are not in a recession but in a deleverage. We haven't had one of those since WW2 so most people don't know what it is and think it is a recession. A deleverage is a once in a 100 year massive transfer of wealth event. I have put resources on what a deleverage is at the end of this reply. The long term problem is that the Fed is a private bank. This means that the US Government and American citizens do not control the Fed. Forget the façade that makes them look like a branch of Government, especially the whole Presidential appointment of the Fed Chairman. It is a private bank that gets to print money and sell it to the US Government that American citizens are forced to use. That means that the US Government and American citizens are slaves with no control over their future. Each dollar printed is a debt burden on the American people and a debasement of the current currency value. Essentially think of printing money as a way that the Fed transfers wealth from your pocket into theirs. Furthermore, I believe that the Fed manipulates the economic cycle to create wealth transfer events that they reap the benefits of. For further information look to the following: [VIDEO] [LINK] www.youtube.com/watch?v=mII9NZ8MMVM‎ [LINK] [LINK]

comments.why_zh: 理解经济如何运转有助于自己管理财务。
comments.quote_zh: 理解经济如何运转[1]
comments.text_zh: 有点离谱的是，至少在美国，中小学几乎不教个人理财。我现在快三十岁了，不得不读了很多资料、做了很多研究，才搞明白该怎么管理工作时拿到的 RSU，以及如何为买房和退休做规划。结果发现（并不意外），大多数金融机构并没有把普通投资者的利益放在心上。相反，它们把我们看成可以在很长一段时间里慢慢榨取价值的客户。理解经济如何运转[1]、金融服务公司如何卖产品、波动与市场力量背后的理论，以及简单的组合管理怎么做，这些对提升个人高效自我管理财务的能力大有帮助。1. [VIDEO]
comments.text: It's kind of crazy that, at least in the US, personal finance is not taught so much in grade school. I had to do a lot of reading and research now in my late twenties to figure out the best way to manage the RSUs I get at work and how to plan for a home purchase and retirement. It turns out (surprise) that most financial institutions don't have regular investors' best interest in mind. Instead, they see us as customers with value to siphon out over long periods of time. Understanding how economies work[1], how financial service companies sell products, theories behind volatility and market forces, and how simple portfolio management can be goes a long way to improving an individuals ability to efficiently self-manage their finances. 1. [VIDEO]

comments.story_title: Nassim Taleb: Bitcoin failed as a currency and became a speculative ponzi scheme
comments.why_zh: 说明了增长来自投资和债务。
comments.quote_zh: Ray Dalio 解释得很好。
comments.text_zh: 历史上，物物交换和市场中使用过各种各样的物品。[LINK] 其中一些，比如牲畜，贬值非常快，因为它们字面意义上是有寿命的。另一些，比如稀有硬币，则升值了。在 Bitcoin 的语境下，我们谈论的是现代世界。现代世界的主要力量是全球化和技术。假设你不想让中国接管世界，你就需要增长。增长发生在投资和债务被创造出来的时候。Ray Dalio 解释得很好。[VIDEO] 这就是为什么像美国这样成功的国家以 2-3% 的通胀为目标。理论上可以创造一个通胀率为 -1% 的国家，但很难阻止的技术增长会制造通缩螺旋，使经济停滞。
comments.text: Historically, there have been a wide range of items used in barter and markets. [LINK] . Some of those like livestock depreciated in value very quickly since they literally had a lifespan. Others, like rare coins have gone up in value. In the context of Bitcoin we are talking about the modern world. The major forces in the modern world are Globalization and Technology. Assuming you don't want China to take over the world you need growth. Growth happens when investment and debts are created. Ray Dalio explains it well. [VIDEO] This is why successful countries like the USA target 2-3% inflation. It is theoretically possible to create a country where inflation was -1%, but technological growth, which is very hard to stop would create a deflationary spiral that would bring the economy to a halt.

comments.author: EGreg
comments.story_title: Voyager suspends trading, deposits, withdrawals, and loyalty rewards
comments.why_zh: 提供了一种了解这一切如何运作的方式。
comments.quote_zh: 了解这一切如何运作
comments.text_zh: 30 年减半？那相当不错！Ethereum 几周内就跌了这么多。牛市上涨时一切都很美好，但熊市里，这些东西可能跌得很惨。货币逐渐贬值——Demurrage——会让人真正去花钱，而不是囤钱。如果你想让钱生息，就得承担一些风险。投资一些资产。通常是股票、房地产，或者（终于多亏了 JOBS act）新创企业。我不明白为什么人们要有“肥厚的银行账户”。钱本来就不是用来储存的。那是银行搞的骗局，连同“你必须买房而不是租房”的观念一起。如果你可以租房，并买入你比房地产更了解的其他资产，那就这么做。这不是魔法……钱总得有个来源。它通常来自银行本身——银行把钱借给那些相信自己能还回更多钱的人和企业！要让所有人能偿还比现有货币总量更多的钱，唯一办法就是在此期间增加货币供应。所以通胀就发生了。唯一的替代方案是让很多人违约并重组贷款，从而欠得更少。这就是 Ray Dalio 所说的可能成为“a beautiful deleveraging”的情况。我不买账……想了解这一切如何运作：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Half in 30 years? That’s pretty good! Ethereum fell by that much in a couple weeks. On the way up in a bull market it’s all roses, but in a bear market, these things can crash hard. Money losing value gradually — Demurrage — makes people actually spend money rather than hoard it. If you want the money to earn interest, you will have to take some risk. Invest in some assets. Usually, stocks or real estate or (finally thanks to the JOBS act) new startups. I don’t know why people have “fat bank accounts”. Money isn’t meant to be stored. That’s a racket by the banks, along with the idea that you have to buy a home instead of renting. If you can rent and buy other assets that you understand better than real estate, then do that. This is not magic .. money has to come from somewhere. It usually comes from banks themselves — who lend it to people and businesses who believe that they can pay back MORE money ! The only way everyone can pay back more money than is in existence is if the money supply is increased in the meantime. So inflation happens. The only alternative is having lots of people default and restructure their loans to owe less. This is what Ray Dalio says can be “a beautiful deleveraging”. I don’t buy it… Learn how it all works: [VIDEO]

comments.story_title: No one is disrupting banks – at least not the big ones
comments.why_zh: 对信用与货币还算过得去的解释。
comments.quote_zh: Ray Dalio 在这里有个还算过得去的解释
comments.text_zh: 接着你房子那个例子往下推。设想在每一个环节，人们不是通过银行账户转账，而是靠信用来完成这些工作。把链条末端所有的信用加起来。然后再回去把“用转账付款”情形下所有银行账户余额加起来。你会发现是一样的（除了那部分准备金）。现在，去看看一堆上市公司的资产负债表——从矿业公司到零售商，一路下来你都会看到应付账款和应收账款。一条长长的信用链。它们本来也可以全都向银行借钱，从而整条链上都没有应收账款。所谓“货币创造”的意义在于让经济活动得以发生。信用做的是同一件事。事实上，你银行里的“钱”只不过是银行欠你的应收账款。Ray Dalio 在这里有个还算过得去的解释：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Continue down the chain on your house example. Imagine in each case instead of transferring money in bank accounts, people do the work on credit. Add up all the credit at the end of the chain. Then go back and add up all the bank account balances in the "pay with money transfer". It'll be the same (except for the fraction). Now, go look at a bunch of public company balance sheets - you'll see payables and receivables all the way down from mining companies to retailers. One long chain of credit. They could have all borrowed money from banks instead and have zero trade receivables throughout the entire chain. The point of "money creation" is to enable economic activity. Credit does the same thing. In fact, your "money" at the bank is just a receivable from the bank. Ray Dalio has a quarter decent explanation of it here: [VIDEO]

comments.author: rglover
comments.story_title: The Dead Economy Theory
comments.why_zh: 让评论者不再以经济恐慌的方式思考。
comments.quote_zh: 让我不再用“糟了，经济不行了，快恐慌”的方式思考
comments.text_zh: “经济”不过是我们用来指代彼此之间进行交易的一个词。无论是个体、企业，还是两者的组合。流行文化中存在的那个“经济”，不过是一种工具，用来敲打人们、让他们接受自己在社会中预先被安排好的角色/等级（并温和地“助推”他们的决策，使其顺从于更大、更富有的实体/个人）。它是吉拉尔式的替罪羊，被设计出来当作靶子，承载人们对不可预测、不可知的未来所有可预见的怨愤与困惑。让我不再用“糟了，经济不行了，快恐慌”的方式思考，而更多转向“好，那你打算怎么办”的，是这个[1]。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: "The economy" is just the word we use for transacting between one another. Whether individuals, or businesses, or a combination. The economy as it exists in popular culture is just a tool to bludgeon people over the head into acceptance of their pre-determined role/rank in society (and softly "nudge" their decision making in the direction of submission to larger, more wealthy entities/individuals). It's a Girard-style scapegoat designed to be a target for all of the predictable vitriol and confusion of an unpredictable and unknowable future. The thing that helped me think less in terms of "oh no the economy is bad, panic" and more so in "okay, what are you going to do about it" was this [1]. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 描述美联储的两个杠杆。
comments.quote_zh: 美联储引导经济所用的两个杠杆——印钞和降息（正如 Ray Dalio 所描述的
comments.text_zh: 我当时在说美联储引导经济所用的两个杠杆——印钞和降息（正如 Ray Dalio 所描述的 [VIDEO]）。我同事眼睛一亮，看着我说：“那量化宽松呢？”我回答说，那就是印钞。我觉得问题在于，这些概念被赋予了听起来很复杂的名词，所以人们不会去质疑它们的伦理。我不是说它们不需要——在信用经济里，它们似乎绝对必要，但也许可以用一种不那么偏向富人的方式来实施。
comments.text: I was talking about the two levers the Fed has to guide the economy at work - Printing Money and Lowering interest rates (as described by Ray Dalio [VIDEO] ). My coworker starry eyed, looked at me and said, "What about Quantitative Easing?". I responded that is printing money. I think the issue is, these concepts are given difficult sounding names, so people do not question their ethics. I'm not saying they are not needed - in a credit based economy it seems they are absolutely necessary, but perhaps they could be implemented in a way that doesn't so favor the rich.

comments.text: > if you were given the choice of having two currencies If having = "to personally own with the hopes that the price goes up", then you pick a currency with limited supply.
